SUBTAREA T3 — Parte 3 — ¿Recupera LDA los temas reales?
Objetivo: Con el modelo de tres temas de la Parte 1, asignar a cada uno de los doce documentos su tema dominante (mayor probabilidad documento-tema). Calcular la pureza: para cada tema de LDA, contar los documentos de la etiqueta real más frecuente entre los asignados a él, sumar esas cuentas y dividir por 12. Producir la tabla de asignación por documento (id, etiqueta real, tema LDA dominante) e identificar qué documentos quedan mal agrupados.

[corpus · blei-2003-lda.pdf, p. 4] (papers del corpus, 2 entidades compartidas)
BLEI, NG, AND JORDAN We wish to find a probabilistic model of a corpus that not only assigns high probability to members of the corpus, but also assigns high probability to other “similar” documents. 3. Latent Dirichlet allocation Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) is a generative probabilistic model of a corpus. The basic idea is that documents are represented as random mixtures over latent topics, where each topic is charac- terized by a distribution over words.1 LDA assumes the following generative process for each document w in a corpus D: 1. Choose N ∼Poisson(ξ). 2. Choose θ ∼Dir(α). 3. For each of the N words wn: (a) Choose a topic zn ∼Multinomial(θ). (b) Choose a word wn from p(wn |zn,β), a multinomial probability conditioned on the topic zn. Several simplifying assumptions are made in this basic model, some of which we remove in subse- quent sections. First, the dimensionality k of the Dirichlet distribution (and thus the dimensionality of the topic variable z) is assumed known and fixed. Second, the word probabilities are parameter- ized by a k ×V matrix β where βij = p(wj = 1|zi = 1), which for now we treat as a fixed quantity that is to be estimated. Finally, the Poisson assumption is not critical to anything that follows and more realistic document length distributions can be used as needed. Furthermore, note that N is independent of all the other data generating variables (θ and z). It is thus an ancillary variable and we will generally ignore its randomness in the subsequent development. A k-dimensional Dirichlet random variable θ can take values in the (k −1)-simplex (a k-vector θ lies in the (k−1)-simplex if θi ≥0, ∑k i=1 θi = 1), and has the following probability density on this simplex: p(θ|α) = Γ �∑k i=1 αi

[corpus · blei-2003-lda.pdf, p. 20] (papers del corpus, 2 entidades compartidas)
BLEI, NG, AND JORDAN each mixture component. When determining the probability of a new document through marginal- ization, only those training documents which exhibit a similar proportion of topics will contribute to the likelihood. For a given training document’s topic proportions, any word which has small probability in all the constituent topics will cause the perplexity to explode. As k gets larger, the chance that a training document will exhibit topics that cover all the words in the new document decreases and thus the perplexity grows. Note that pLSI does not overfit as quickly (with respect to k) as the mixture of unigrams. This overfitting problem essentially stems from the restriction that each future document exhibit the same topic proportions as were seen in one or more of the training documents. Given this constraint, we are not free to choose the most likely proportions of topics for the new document. An alternative approach is the “folding-in” heuristic suggested by Hofmann (1999), where one ignores the p(z|d) parameters and refits p(z|dnew). Note that this gives the pLSI model an unfair advantage by allowing it to refit k −1 parameters to the test data. LDA suffers from neither of these problems. As in pLSI, each document can exhibit a different proportion of underlying topics. However, LDA can easily assign probability to a new document; no heuristics are needed for a new document to be endowed with a different set of topic proportions than were associated with documents in the training corpus. Figure 9 presents the perplexity for each model on both corpora for different values of k. The pLSI model and mixture of unigrams are suitably corrected for overfitting.
```python
import json
import numpy as np
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
from sklearn.decomposition import LatentDirichletAllocation

# Corpus mínimo del enunciado: 12 documentos, 3 temas reales
corpus = [
    ("d01", "El delantero marcó dos goles en el partido de fútbol y el equipo ganó la liga.", "deporte"),
    ("d02", "El entrenador del equipo preparó la defensa para el partido final de la liga.", "deporte"),
    ("d03", "La tenista ganó el torneo después de un partido largo contra la campeona.", "deporte"),
    ("d04", "El equipo de baloncesto perdió el partido por un punto en el último segundo.", "deporte"),
    ("d05", "La receta lleva harina, huevos y azúcar; la masa se hornea durante treinta minutos.", "cocina"),
    ("d06", "Para la salsa se sofríe cebolla y ajo en aceite y se añade tomate.", "cocina"),
    ("d07", "El pan se hornea con harina, agua, sal y levadura después de amasar la masa.", "cocina"),
    ("d08", "La sopa de verduras lleva cebolla, zanahoria, ajo y sal, y se cocina a fuego lento.", "cocina"),
    ("d09", "El telescopio observó una galaxia lejana y varias estrellas de la nebulosa.", "astronomía"),
    ("d10", "Los planetas giran alrededor de la estrella; la órbita de la Tierra dura un año.", "astronomía"),
    ("d11", "La nebulosa es una nube de gas donde nacen estrellas nuevas en la galaxia.", "astronomía"),
    ("d12", "El telescopio espacial fotografió planetas y la órbita de una luna de Júpiter.", "astronomía"),
]
ids = [c[0] for c in corpus]
textos = [c[1] for c in corpus]
etiquetas = [c[2] for c in corpus]

stop_words = ["el", "la", "los", "las", "de", "del", "en", "y", "a", "un", "una", "por",
              "para", "con", "se", "su", "al", "es", "después", "durante", "contra",
              "donde", "alrededor"]

# Refit del modelo de la Parte 1 (mismos parámetros; determinista con random_state=0)
vec = CountVectorizer(stop_words=stop_words)
X = vec.fit_transform(textos)
lda = LatentDirichletAllocation(n_components=3, learning_method="batch", max_iter=50, random_state=0)
lda.fit(X)

doc_topic = lda.transform(X)  # probabilidades documento-tema (12 x 3)
tema_dom = doc_topic.argmax(axis=1)

# Pureza: por tema LDA, cuenta de la etiqueta real más frecuente entre sus documentos
resumen_temas = {}
acierto = 0
for t in range(3):
    idx = np.where(tema_dom == t)[0]
    cuentas = {}
    for i in idx:
        cuentas[etiquetas[i]] = cuentas.get(etiquetas[i], 0) + 1
    if cuentas:
        etiq_mayor = max(cuentas, key=cuentas.get)
        n_mayor = cuentas[etiq_mayor]
    else:
        etiq_mayor, n_mayor = None, 0
    resumen_temas[str(t)] = {"etiqueta_mayoritaria": etiq_mayor,
                             "cuenta_mayoritaria": int(n_mayor),
                             "total_documentos": int(len(idx)),
                             "cuentas_por_etiqueta": cuentas}
    acierto += n_mayor
pureza = acierto / 12.0

asignacion = []
mal_agrupados = []
for i, did in enumerate(ids):
    t = int(tema_dom[i])
    etiq_mayor = resumen_temas[str(t)]["etiqueta_mayoritaria"]
    bien = etiquetas[i] == etiq_mayor
    asignacion.append({"id": did,
                       "etiqueta_real": etiquetas[i],
                       "tema_lda_dominante": t,
                       "prob_doc_tema": [float(p) for p in doc_topic[i]],
                       "etiqueta_mayoritaria_del_tema": etiq_mayor,
                       "bien_agrupado": bool(bien)})
    if not bien:
        mal_agrupados.append(did)

# Verificación ligera contra la Parte 1 (tamaño del vocabulario)
coincide_t1 = None
try:
    with open("entradas/T1.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        t1 = json.load(f)
    coincide_t1 = bool(int(X.shape[1]) == int(t1["tamano_vocabulario"]))
except Exception:
    pass

resultados = {"asignacion_por_documento": asignacion,
              "pureza": float(pureza),
              "documentos_mal_agrupados": mal_agrupados,
              "resumen_temas": resumen_temas,
              "tamano_vocabulario": int(X.shape[1]),
              "coincide_vocab_con_T1": coincide_t1}
with open("resultados.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(resultados, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

print("Tabla de asignación (id | etiqueta real | tema LDA dominante | probs doc-tema | bien agrupado):")
for a in asignacion:
    print(f"  {a['id']} | {a['etiqueta_real']:<10} | tema {a['tema_lda_dominante']} | "
          f"{[round(p, 4) for p in a['prob_doc_tema']]} | {a['bien_agrupado']}")
print(f"Pureza: {pureza}")
print(f"Documentos mal agrupados: {mal_agrupados}")
print(f"Tamaño del vocabulario: {X.shape[1]} (coincide con T1: {coincide_t1})")

```
